summary: Short seller training (03:23) on the cancellation policy that, at the time of recording, Revibe had 'just launched'. A customer cancels either because they changed their mind or because the shipment is delayed on the seller's side. The cancelled order then has a small purple bar on the left of its row in the orders list. Inside the order, a banner says the order is on hold, and the trainer says it cannot be edited. A Cancellation claim (Stage 'To be cancelled') is created. The seller opens the claim from the order's Claims section and has two choices. Mark valid accepts: the order is cancelled and the customer refunded. Mark Invalid rejects. With no response within 24 hours, the cancellation is treated as valid. For UAE and South Africa, a cancellation at the Created stage must always be accepted. At the quality check stage it can be rejected, but the seller must then ship within the next 24 hours. Saudi Arabia orders can always be rejected, with the same 24-hour shipping duty. The trainer says marking a cancellation invalid requires a tracking ID, but his line about which countries this applies to is ambiguous. In the demo, Mark Invalid on a United Arab Emirates order with no tracking ID showed the error 'Tracking ID is required to mark the claim as invalid' and an 'Add tracking ID' pop-up. If the tracking ID is already there, the seller can just press invalid. After a rejection the order shows again as a normal, editable order, but this was only said, not shown. The demo was recorded on an admin dashboard at stage-admin.revibe.me.

terms.meaning: The claim created when a customer cancels an order. It shows in the order's Claims section with Type 'Cancellation' (Stage 'To be cancelled', Status 'Open' while pending), and the seller must respond to it.
The state of an order after the customer cancels it. A banner says 'This order is currently on hold', and the trainer says the seller cannot edit the order and needs to respond to the claim.
The trainer's name for the small purple bar on the left edge of an order row in the orders list, marking an order the customer has cancelled.
Accept the cancellation. The order is cancelled and the customer is refunded. If the seller does not respond within 24 hours, the cancellation is treated as if marked valid.
Reject the cancellation. The seller must then ship within the next 24 hours. The trainer says a tracking ID is required unless it is already on the order. Which countries this covers is ambiguous.
An order stage named by the trainer. For UAE and South Africa, a cancellation at this stage must always be accepted.
An order stage named by the trainer. For UAE and South Africa, a cancellation at this stage may be rejected, provided the order is shipped within the next 24 hours.
The claim Stage shown on a pending customer cancellation.
Claim Subtype shown on the demo cancellation, matching the 'customer changed his mind' scenario.

The shipment tracking reference. In the demo it had to be entered in the 'Add tracking ID' pop-up before the cancellation could be marked invalid. The trainer says this is not needed if the order already has one.

unclear.issue: The line 'This you will have to do it for Saudi Arabia orders only, for UAE and South Africa orders.' contradicts itself. One possible reading, given the trainer's French phrasing and the pauses: 'You have to input a tracking ID for Saudi Arabia orders only. For UAE and South Africa orders, if the tracking ID is already here you can just press invalid.' That would tie the 02:31 tip to UAE/South Africa. Other readings are that the tracking ID is required for all three countries, or 'not for UAE and South Africa'. On screen, the demo order (Country 'United Arab Emirates', t00044; Tracking ID '-', t00000) did get the error 'Tracking ID is required to mark the claim as invalid' (t00139). Confirm with the trainer which countries require a tracking ID to reject.

'you won't need to put tracking ID link' is garbled. 'link' may be a mishearing, perhaps of 'again' or 'in'. The meaning that no tracking ID needs entering if one is already on the order is clear. Whether a link (URL) rather than an ID is ever expected is not.

The demo was recorded on stage-admin.revibe.me, an admin dashboard whose left menu shows admin items ('User Manag...', 'Roles Mana...', 'Claim Mana...', 'Payment Tool', 'Invoices', 'Order Views ...', 'Claim Views ...', 'Logs'). The trainer, however, talks to sellers about 'your orders app'. The seller's own view may look different and may not show buttons such as Mark Refunded or Cancel override.

The trainer says an on-hold order cannot be edited, yet the order panel header shows an 'Edit' button while the on-hold banner is displayed (t00044, t00052, t00056). This may be because the demo is in the admin view. It is not shown what happens if a seller tries to edit.
Not covered: what happens if a seller rejects a cancellation but does not ship within the 24 hours.
Not covered: for UAE and South Africa, only the Created stage (must accept) and the quality check stage (may reject) are mentioned. Cancellations at other stages are not addressed.
The Mark Refunded and Cancel override buttons appear on the Claim Details tab but are never explained.

outdated.signal: The trainer calls it 'the new cancellation policy that we just launched'. The demo claim is dated 2025-05-19 (t00044), so the policy is from around May 2025. Check that the 24-hour rules and the country/stage rules still apply.
